name: Financial Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 8

book.title: The Penguin Book of Financial Times Crosswords, volume 1

blocks.note: to forge is to counterfeit
any letter will do; here the twentieth of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A faked letter written to excuse someone's failure to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is vague on purpose: the solver chooses whichever letter completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect a duty is to fail to remember or attend to it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: In which jockeys jostle for accommodation?

definitions.text: In which jockeys jostle for accommodation?

blocks.note: reads like riders fighting over somewhere to live
the setter means a horse race run without jumps, an apartment being a kind of lodging

explanation.walkthrough: An apartment is a kind of accommodation, so jockeys 'jostling for' one becomes a race on level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race run over level ground with no fences or hurdles, where riders compete for position.

clue.text: Don't dig so much being on the move

blocks.note: first meaning: an order to grub about in the soil less, as a pig would with its snout
second meaning: having no settled home

explanation.surface: A gardener told to dig less now that they are moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer without settled home or ties is described as lacking roots, an adjective sense.

clue.text: She is Eastern, high class, and pleasant

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for East
U is the British label for upper-class usage
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A description of a refined, agreeable woman from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name stands in for the pronoun, a typical crossword way to clue first names.

blocks.note: re means concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A cross-reference telling you to look up a writer on beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a writer of what is seen: a journalist covering events at first hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist describes events witnessed in person, so an eyewitness author is this newspaper role.

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: Vestments being brought out for an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor is the Latin abbreviation the Archbishop of York uses when signing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs with his see's Latin abbreviation, so the name stands for that prelate.

blocks.note: reads as a question about Queen Mary, the Dutch king's consort
the setter means the cockney slang for one's wife, fitting a Dutchman's spouse

explanation.walkthrough: In cockney slang 'my old Dutch' means my wife; William of Orange was Dutch, so his wife is literally that.
explanation.definitionFit: London rhyming-slang style term of endearment for a long-married spouse, from the music-hall song.

clue.text: '—rank and_gross in nature Possess it utterly' (Hamlet)

definitions.text: '—rank and_gross in nature Possess it utterly' (Hamlet)

blocks.clueFragment: '—rank and_gross in nature Possess it utterly'
blocks.note: a quotation with its first word missing
the source: Hamlet's first soliloquy, where the world is an unweeded garden

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the gap from Hamlet's soliloquy: the unweeded garden is possessed by these rank, gross growths. Shakespeare wrote 'merely' where this copy prints 'utterly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the plural noun the speaker uses for the weeds choking the garden.

blocks.note: alludes to Hogarth's series of paintings about a dissolute young man's downfall
the setter means a jaunty tilt, as a hat worn at a dashing slant

explanation.walkthrough: The word describes both a rake's dissolute manner and a hat set at a jaunty angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocked hat worn at a dashing slant is said to sit this way, and the adjective also means dissolute.

blocks.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Someone asking the price of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like haggling at a horse sale, but 'How much' is a noun phrase for a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity or sum answers the question of how much there is of something.

blocks.note: a hood is a gangster
a wink is a signal

explanation.surface: A con trick worked with a crook's secret signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick or dupe someone is to deceive them, a straightforward verb synonym.

blocks.note: the Port of London Authority, the body managing the Thames
a card is an eccentric person, a character

explanation.surface: A river authority's notice board with lettering on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The PLA (Port of London Authority) runs the tidal Thames, hence a 'river board'.
explanation.definitionFit: A poster or notice put up for public view, carried at protests or fixed to walls, is a display.

clue.text: Muster the diner's first course demand

blocks.note: a bread roll is eaten first at dinner
a call for something is a demand

explanation.surface: A diner insisting on the starter being served.
explanation.walkthrough: The bread roll served at the start of a meal is the 'first course' here, not soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A muster is an assembly of troops checked by reading names aloud, the same as a roll-call.

clue.text: Moves when I abandon the birds

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written; this is the letter removed
budgies are budgerigars, small parrots

explanation.surface: Someone shifts when the pet birds are left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from BUDGIES to leave BUDGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift position slightly, so it is a verb synonym of moves.

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
taken as written
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Hailing a taxi for government officials.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior government ministers who meet with the prime minister form this collective body.

blocks.note: first meaning: a form for shaping metal, or to shape it
second meaning: the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Shaping the members of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundry shapes metal in moulds, and a theatre company's assembled actors are likewise named by this word.

clue.text: It hurts to quit the tournament

blocks.note: first meaning: a small wound from a claw or thorn
second meaning: to withdraw an entrant from a competition

explanation.surface: A player pulling out of a competition because of the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor graze stings, and withdrawing an entry from a race or contest is the sporting verb sense.

clue.text: Made a noise like Shelley's noontide bee

definitions.text: Made a noise like Shelley's noontide bee

blocks.note: a literary allusion to a bee in Shelley's verse
the setter means the low continuous hum of a bee, in the past tense

explanation.walkthrough: Shelley wrote of the 'noontide bee' and its humming; the answer is that soft continuous sound as a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A low indistinct continuous sound, like bees humming or quiet speech, is described by this verb.

blocks.note: reads as something mislaid or someone absorbed
the setter means the word that precedes Lost in Milton's epic poem title

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's epic poem is Paradise Lost; the clue asks for the word that is 'lost' in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic about the Fall of Man is titled with this word followed by the clue's first word.

clue.text: Aped a rep — or so it seemed

indicators.note: 'or so' means something like it, an approximate version, so the letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone imitated a salesman, or so people thought.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the impression of being something is to look or seem so, a past-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: Spirit returns to precipitate foot and mouth

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the spirit is read backwards

blocks.note: rum is a spirit; read backwards
rain is precipitation, and to rain is to precipitate

explanation.surface: Alcohol coming back to bring on an outbreak of disease.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old word for an infectious disease of cattle, such as the plague of hooves and lips.

clue.text: Distort the conflict with soft conclusion

blocks.note: war is armed conflict
p (piano) means soft in music, placed at the end

explanation.surface: Twisting the story of a war so it ends gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend or twist something out of its true shape is to distort it, a verb synonym.

blocks.note: dies are tools for stamping coins or metal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Postage stamps stuck on a Spanish engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A compression-ignition motor, or a locomotive driven by one, is named after its German inventor.

blocks.note: first meaning: to scale a wall is to climb it
second meaning: what covers a fish's skin

explanation.surface: Someone clambering over people in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The swimmers' does not define the answer directly: fish are the swimmers, and the answer is what they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascending a wall or cliff is scaling it, and the protective plates on fish give the same word.

blocks.note: Di's, belonging to Di, a girl's name
one's own is one's property

explanation.surface: Refusing a young woman what belongs to her.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to acknowledge any connection with a person or thing is to repudiate or deny them.

clue.text: Suggests entry on the credit side

definitions.text: Suggests entry on the credit side

blocks.note: split into two short words, the answer reads as an invitation to step inside
the whole is money received, recorded on the credit side of the books

explanation.walkthrough: The accounting picture of a ledger entry hides an invitation: split the answer into two short words and it bids you come inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are money received, recorded as credits in an account, the opposite of expenditure.

clue.text: Take tenth of the month I marry

blocks.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
taken as written
to mate is to pair up or wed

explanation.surface: Someone choosing the tenth of December for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenth of the month' looks like a date, but 'of' belongs with 'tenth' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans punished mutinous legions by killing one man in every ten, the original sense of this verb.

blocks.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to see his beloved, a priestess of Aphrodite
the setter means her name is a word for a brave man, which as a woman she could not be

explanation.walkthrough: Leander's lover was the priestess Hero; as a woman she would be called a heroine, so she was not what her name says.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave man admired for courage is the masculine noun, which the woman named this was not.

clue.text: Alas! Dire way to be paid

indicators.note: a way is a manner of doing something, here a new arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lament about a terrible method of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker on a fixed regular wage is paid by salary, so receiving pay fits as an adjective.

clue.text: Better — or more tattered than you?

blocks.note: first meaning: more saintly
second meaning: having more holes, read as 'holey' compared

explanation.surface: A sneer at someone who thinks themselves superior, or merely more ragged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Than you' nods to the idiom 'holier than thou', for a self-righteous person.
explanation.definitionFit: More virtuous means morally superior, while a garment full of holes is more ragged; the spelling serves both.

blocks.note: reads like the final letter of a word, or the edge of a city
the setter means the excellent final bit of a drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the old exclamation for excellent; the clue praises the final mouthful of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The final swallow left in a glass is the closing portion of any beverage, often savoured.

blocks.note: un is French for a
a bend is a curve

explanation.surface: Easing into a graceful French curve.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen up and become less stiff or formal is to relax, a verb synonym.
